title.narrative: Contribution to AILAC administered by UNDP

description.narrative:
The Independent Association of Latin America and the Caribbean (AILAC) consists of eight countries (Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay and Peru) that have common interests and positions related to climate change.
By contributing to the AILAC secretariat with 5 million DKK in 2024, Denmark will support the progressive Latin American countries in the COP negotiations and other climate fora and build bridges to ambitious G77 countries, in line with Danish priorities. Colombia no longer holds the pro tempore presidency of AILAC, but nevertheless prioritises international support to the Secretariat. In 2024, Honduras and Panama will hold the presidency. A Danish contribution can help build strong relations with Colombia, Panama and other strategic partners in the region on the climate agenda and strengthen the Danish profile as a bridge builder between the Global North and South for the climate negotiations.
The Danish contribution will be administered by UNDP through their Progressive Platforms, which is part of the flagship project, Climate Promise. The platform is multi-donor funded and is planned to operate for the period 2023-2026. The main purpose is to support various progressive entities and groups to, among other things, ensure engagement in the UNFCCC processes and ultimately the achievement of the Paris Agreement.
The Danish support is earmarked for specific activities in 2024 agreed between Denmark and AILAC with assistance from UNDP in accordance with the OECD DAC guidelines for development assistance. The contribution is implemented from § 06.38.02.18. The SDG Facility, which the Embassy in Colombia has access to in its role as a climate frontpost.
